title: Executive Brief
body:
How to use this plan This document is the operating blueprint for HighLife from August 2026 through the end of 2027. It is designed to answer five questions every week: What are we trying to build? What number are we chasing? What work matters now? Who owns it? What tells us whether it is working?
The plan in one page Decision HighLife operating answer North Star Build a globally relevant creative company under one umbrella: Music, Media and Merch, with events and community as connective tissue.
2027 financial goal $250K cumulative revenue from Aug. 10, 2026 through Dec.
31, 2027. Operate toward a $20K-$25K monthly exit run-rate.
Primary growth bet Podcast production and recurring media services. Treat podcasting as the cash engine inside the Media pillar.
Current baseline ~$9K/month: roughly $8K music studio and $1K podcast.
Resource allocation Approximately 65% podcast/revenue growth, 15% music, 10% HighLife media brand, 10% merch/events experiments.
Leadership cadence Monday 10:00 AM business meeting; Wednesday 5:30 PM team meeting; Sunday 4:00 PM brand meeting.
Content cadence HL Podcast weekly; podcast commercials 2x/month; HL Freestyle 1x/month on Saturday; one event/month, eventually two.
Systems HighLevel owns leads and customers. HighLife Roadmap owns execution, OKRs, owners, deadlines and SOPs.
Document map STRATEGY
• North Star and five-year vision
• Current-state diagnosis
• Revenue path and portfolio logic
• Podcast offer and ICP
• Growth funnel and sales system OPERATIONS
• Weekly and monthly cadence
• Quarterly OKRs
• KPI scorecard
• Team and hiring triggers
• Roadmap, SOPs and 90-day execution plan The core management rule Do not make every HighLife pillar equal priority every week. Keep all three alive, but concentrate growth resources on the one engine with the highest revenue ceiling: podcasting.

title: North Star
body:
The five-year vision HighLife is not trying to remain only a recording studio. The five-year ambition is a globally relevant creative company with dominance across three connected pillars: Music, Media and Merch. Events and community are the distribution layer that make the three pillars feel like one culture instead of separate businesses.
5-YEAR NORTH STAR Global cultural relevance through Music + Media + Merch, built under one HighLife umbrella.
What each pillar is responsible for Pillar Role in the ecosystem Near-term job MUSIC Cultural engine Protect the existing studio base, technical reputation, engineers, artist community and creative credibility.
MEDIA Cash + audience engine Scale podcast production first; use owned HighLife content to grow authority and distribution.
MERCH Commerce + identity engine Build slowly through limited drops, collaborations and event-linked validation instead of inventory-heavy bets.
EVENTS Community connector Create revenue, leads, content and community moments that feed all three pillars.
Values that should survive the scale HighLife already publicly defines four values: Artist First, Fearless Creativity, Respect & Integrity, and Adapt & Innovate. The growth plan should strengthen those values, not replace them with a generic corporate culture.
WHAT HIGH LIFE SHOULD BECOME
• The DMV creative home for serious artists and media creators
• A full-service media partner for established professionals and brands
• An owned media platform with recognizable shows and formats
• A consumer-facing brand whose merch and events mean something WHAT HIGH LIFE SHOULD NOT BECOME
• A cheap room-rental marketplace
• A content agency that says yes to every project
• A meeting-heavy company with no scoreboard
• A business that burns cash chasing every creative idea at once Source note: HighLife public story, values and community pages reviewed August 10, 2026.

title: Current State
body:
The business today: strong product, underbuilt revenue engine $9K AVERAGE MONTHLY REVENUE Current baseline ~$8K MUSIC STUDIO Current primary revenue ~$1K PODCAST Largest room for growth 10 PODCAST TOURS Booked in one recent week What is already working  Established HighLife brand, physical studios, technical team, interns and engineers already in place.
 Podcast suite has one room with 3-4 set configurations, multi-camera equipment, microphones, lighting and production staff.
 Public pricing is premium enough to support a high-value model: video podcast production starts at $300/hour while music sessions are typically around $60-$75/hour depending on location.
 HighLife already offers the full post-production stack: video editing, audio editing, short-form clips, mixing/mastering and on-location recording.
 New marketing/sales partner operates ads, AI outbound, CRM automation and HighLevel; compensation is 15% of the first collected sale.
 Initial demand signal is promising: 10 podcast tours booked in one recent week, the strongest tour volume to date.
The diagnosis Constraint Reality Management response Music capacity Current hourly music model likely tops out around $10K-$12K/month.
Protect it; do not expect it to carry the growth target.
Podcast capacity Only one room, but it is currently far from a near-term revenue bottleneck. Fill the room before discussing expansion.
Sales Historically barren; now the new marketing engine is generating tours.
Shift attention from lead generation alone to conversion, recurring packages and retention.
Leadership Jaco + JoJo are the only high-level business leaders today.
Keep decision-making tight; add fractional/contract leverage by trigger, not titles.
Execution Many creative priorities can compete for attention.
Use one weekly cadence, three quarterly OKRs and the Roadmap as the source of truth.
Key conclusion The 2026-2027 problem is not "we need more services." HighLife already has the service stack. The problem is turning demand into a repeatable sales-to-recurring-revenue machine.

title: Revenue Architecture
body:
The $250K path The official goal is cumulative revenue from now through the end of 2027, not a single-year $250K run-rate. The base plan below reaches exactly $250K. HighLife should still manage internally toward a stretch result so one weak month does not break the goal.
$250K OFFICIAL FLOOR Cumulative by Dec. 31, 2027 $275K INTERNAL STRETCH Recommended management buffer $20K-$25K EXIT RUN-RATE Target range by late 2027 Base monthly revenue targets are deliberately achievable. They require HighLife to grow from roughly $9K/month today to $19K/month by December 2027, while the $25K/month number remains a stretch exit target rather than the minimum required path.

Q4 2026 $36K $52K Exit December at ~$13K/month with podcast becoming material.
Q1 2027 $43K $95K Build retention and recurring podcast book.
Q2 2027 $47K $142K Scale channels beyond paid ads and harden delivery capacity.

Recommended late-2027 revenue mix Line Base expectation Stretch expectation Why Music studio $8K-$10K/mo $10K-$12K/mo Stable cultural and cash base;
hourly ceiling remains real.
Podcast/media $9K-$11K/mo $12K-$15K+/mo Primary scalable engine through recording + post + recurring packages.
Events + merch + other $1K-$2K/mo $2K-$4K/mo Variable; should support brand and acquisition without becoming a distraction.
Important finance distinction Track both booked revenue and cash collected, but use cash collected for the revenue scoreboard. Pipeline value is not revenue. MRR is contracted recurring monthly value. Profit is not revenue.

title: Portfolio Focus
body:
Do not split attention evenly Area Share of growth attention What "good" looks like Podcast / revenue growth 65% Ads, AI outbound, tours, sales, recurring packages, retention, referrals, partnerships and premium production delivery.
Music 15% Protect $8K-ish base, engineer quality, client retention, community, monthly freestyle and selective upsells.
HighLife media brand 10% Weekly HL Podcast, proof content, founder/brand stories and assets that feed organic demand.

Area Share of growth attention What "good" looks like Merch + events 10% One monthly event and controlled merch tests tied to community moments, preorders or collaborations.
The operating flywheel Step What happens
1. Acquire Ads + AI outbound + partnerships + organic content generate qualified leads and tours.
2. Convert Tour experience and fast proposals turn leads into paid first sessions or packages.
3. Retain Great production, editing, reserved slots and client success turn first sales into recurring MRR.
4. Capture Every client, event and HighLife-owned show creates proof, clips, testimonials and relationships.
5. Reinvest Podcast profit funds better media, music, events and merch, which increases HighLife relevance and demand.
Management principle Revenue funds relevance. Relevance should then make revenue cheaper to acquire. If an initiative does neither, it should not be a priority this quarter.

title: Podcast Revenue Engine
body:
Sell the show, not the room hour HighLife can continue advertising a $300/hour video podcast session, but the internal sales goal should be recurring full-service relationships. Established clients are not buying cameras and microphones; they are buying a professional media presence without having to build and manage a production team.
Current public service stack Service Current public pricing snapshot Strategic role Video podcast production Starting at $300/hour Premium capture product and top-of- funnel anchor.
Audio podcast production Starting at $100/hour Lower-complexity option; not the main growth engine.
Video editing Up to 60 min: $350; 60-90 min: $450 Highest-value post-production upsell and recurring deliverable.
Audio editing Up to 60 min: $200 Useful for audio distribution and polished deliverables.
Mixing & mastering Up to 2 hours: $200 Quality and consistency upsell.
Short-form clips 3 clips: $150 Growth deliverable; easy recurring bundle component.
On-location recording Custom quote High-value corporate, event and executive opportunity.
Pricing source: HighLife public podcast page reviewed August 10, 2026. The pricing calculator is a dynamic quote tool and should remain the operational quote surface while package architecture is refined.
Why podcast economics deserve disproportionate focus 4.3x ROOM-HOUR PRICE ~$300 podcast vs. ~$70 music $800 ILLUSTRATIVE EPISODE 1 hr + edit + 3 clips $3.2K ILLUSTRATIVE WEEKLY CLIENT 4 full-service episodes/month Illustrative math: one 1-hour video episode at $300 + a <=60-minute video edit at $350 + three short clips at $150 = $800 gross revenue before optional audio work or other add-ons. Four episodes per month = $3,200. This is revenue math, not profit math; editor labor and production costs must be tracked.

Recommended recurring package architecture Offer Recommended price Designed for Core scope Studio Session $300/hr One-off or trial clients Video capture with HighLife production team; raw files; upsell post-production.
Biweekly Authority $1,750/mo Established professionals starting a serious show 2 x 1-hour video sessions, 2 full edits, 6 short clips total, reserved scheduling, standard delivery.
Weekly Authority $3,250/mo Active brands and creators 4 x 1-hour sessions, 4 full edits, 12 short clips, audio polish, priority scheduling.
Executive Media Engine $5,000+/mo HNW, political, medical, corporate or media clients Weekly production plus expanded clip volume, strategy, distribution support, custom graphics and/or on-location options.
Package rule Do not finalize pricing until HighLife measures real editor hours, production labor, revisions, sales commission and payment fees. Bundle convenience, priority and output - not deep discounts. Use 3-month commitments and autopay for recurring packages.
Upsells that increase account value  Additional short-form clips and clip packs.
 Thumbnail and graphic package.
 Audio-only distribution master and platform-ready exports.
 Extra cameras, guests, hours or extended edit length.
 On-location executive, corporate, conference and event recording.
 Commercial or branded content production around the podcast.
 Publishing/distribution support where HighLife has operational capacity.
 Sponsor-message insertion and branded integrations.
Recurring client retention system Moment Standard At close Autopay, term, scope, reserved cadence and deliverable expectations are explicit.
Kickoff One-page show brief: audience, purpose, visual set, cadence, deliverables, approval path.
Every session Producer checks next episode date before client leaves.
Delivery Send assets + next-action note; capture revision reasons to improve process.
Monthly For package clients, review output, upcoming topics and any additional content needs.
After 3 wins Ask for testimonial, referral and/or introduction to another qualified brand.

title: Ideal Customer + Positioning
body:
Broad verticals, narrow buying signals HighLife can serve multiple verticals without marketing to "everyone." The common thread is an established person or organization with a reason to publish consistently, enough budget to value quality, and a desire to avoid building an internal production team.
Primary ICP clusters Cluster Why they buy Best message Business owners / executives Authority, lead generation, recruiting, thought leadership "Turn your expertise into a professional media presence without building a media department." Medical / healthcare leaders Education, credibility, patient/community communication "Studio-grade production with a team that handles the technical complexity." Politics / policy / associations Ideas, constituency, advocacy, visibility "Reliable, professional multi-camera production in the DC market." Established podcasters with weak quality Upgrade visual/audio brand without losing format "Keep your show. Upgrade how the world experiences it." Media personalities / HNW creators Consistency, brand polish, convenience "Show up, record, leave with a production engine behind you." Qualification signals GREEN FLAGS
• Clear reason for the show beyond "I want a podcast"
• Plans to publish at least 2x/month
• Existing business, audience, brand or professional reputation
• Values convenience and production quality
• Decision-maker attends the tour
• Can commit to a 3-month content cadence RED FLAGS
• Pure price shopping
• No publishing plan or topic ownership
• One-off project with no strategic value unless highly profitable
• Expects unlimited edits or undefined deliverables
• No decision authority or budget clarity
• Wants HighLife to invent the entire business/brand before agreeing to scope Core positioning HighLife is the DMV production partner for serious voices: professional video, audio, editing and content support under one roof.
Tour discovery questions
1. Why are you starting or upgrading the show now?
2. Who is the audience and what should the show do for your business or brand?
3. How often do you want to publish?
4. What is hardest about your current process: recording, editing, clips, consistency, distribution or all of it?
5. Who is involved in approving content and budget?
6. What would a great 90 days of content look like?
7. Would you rather manage vendors every episode or have one team own the production system?

title: Sales + Marketing Engine
body:
Make the 10-tour week repeatable The recent 10-tour week is a real signal, but the new scoreboard is not "leads." It is the entire conversion chain:
qualified lead -> showed tour -> paid first sale -> recurring package -> retained client.
HighLevel pipeline Stage Definition Required action / SLA New lead Form, ad, AI outbound response, referral or event lead Immediate automated response; human touch same business day.
Contacted Two-way contact established Qualify need, timing, cadence and decision- maker.
Tour booked Calendar slot confirmed 24-hour + 2-hour reminder; send location/parking/set preview.
Tour showed Qualified person physically/virtually toured Proposal or package options same day.
Proposal sent Scope and price delivered Follow-up Day 1, 3, 7 and 14 unless client replies sooner.
Paid / first session Payment collected and first work booked Onboard and tee up recurring package before delivery.
Recurring offer Client has experienced HighLife and received package option Close cadence, term, autopay and reserved slots.
Recurring active Autopay recurring client Track retention, delivery and expansion.
Nurture / lost Not now, no fit or lost Tag reason; nurture only if legitimate future fit.

Weekly funnel targets - first 90 days Metric Initial target Why it matters Tours booked 8-12/week Preserve current signal and smooth week- to-week variance.
Tour show rate >= 65%, then >= 70% Prevents marketing spend from dying in calendar no-shows.
Tour-to-first-sale close >= 25% Makes the tour a sales asset, not a free visit.
First-sale-to-recurring conversion >= 30%, then 40%+ This is the path to MRR.
Lead response Same business day; automate instantly Speed matters most while intent is high.
Proposal speed Same day Do not let tour excitement decay.
90-day recurring retention >= 80% once enough volume exists Growth fails if recurring clients churn quickly.

Channel strategy Channel Owner Weekly work Scoreboard Paid ads Marketing/sales partner Creative testing, landing page optimization, retargeting, budget control Spend, CPL, qualified tours, CAC, revenue by campaign AI outbound Marketing/sales partner + interns Target lists, personalized outreach, reply handling, booking Contacts, positive replies, booked tours, show rate Referrals Jaco + client success Ask after successful deliveries;
partner with agencies, consultants and communities Introductions, referral sales, partner revenue Organic proof Brand team HL Podcast, client clips, testimonials, BTS, event content Inbound leads and assisted conversions Events Leadership + team Monthly activation with clear business objective P&L, attendees, leads, booked tours, content assets Two commercial shoots per month - what to create Creative type Example angle CTA Proof / testimonial Show a real client transformation, set, final clip or quote Book a tour Quality demonstration Before/after audio, camera angles, lighting, multi-set flexibility See the studio Authority / pain "Your podcast should not look like a Zoom call if your brand is worth millions." Upgrade your show Full-service convenience "Record. We handle the cameras, edit and clips." Request a package quote Each commercial shoot should create multiple hooks and edits rather than one final ad. The marketing team can test persona x hook x offer combinations without requiring new production every week.
Sales compensation rule Keep the 15% first-sale commission for now Pay commission on collected net service revenue after payment clears, not on uncollected quotes. Review the structure after 60-90 days of data. If recurring packages become the priority, consider a small one-time bonus for closing 3-month package commitments rather than paying lifetime residuals.

title: Capacity + Service Operations
body:
One podcast room is enough - for now HighLife has one podcast room and can shoot only one podcast at a time, but that is not currently the limiting factor. At $300/hour, even 10 paid podcast recording hours per week equates to roughly $13K/month of recording revenue before any edits or clips. The near-term challenge is sales, scheduling, post-production and retention - not a second room.
10 HRS/WK PODCAST ROOM USE ~$12.9K/mo recording revenue 15 HRS/WK PODCAST ROOM USE ~$19.4K/mo recording revenue 1 ROOM CURRENT CAPACITY Expand only after threshold is proven Capacity triggers Signal Trigger Action Prime-time room utilization >60% for 8 consecutive weeks Raise/segment pricing, expand hours, tighten recurring reserved slots.
Prime-time room utilization >75% for 8 weeks + meaningful waitlist Begin second-room / alternate-space business case.
Editing backlog Typical delivery repeatedly exceeds 7 business days Add contract editor capacity before adding more marketing volume.
Revisions >20%-25% of jobs require avoidable rework Fix pre-production brief, templates and approval process.
Founder sales load Jaco spends >5 hours/week on routine follow-up for 4+ weeks Add dedicated closer/pipeline coordinator.
Client success load 8-10+ recurring clients and missed follow- ups appear Assign a podcast producer/client success owner.
Service standards  Every recurring show has a one-page production brief and reserved recording cadence.
 Session starts on time; set, cameras, lighting, audio and files are checked before client arrival.
 File naming, storage and handoff follow the same convention every time.
 Post-production scope is explicit before the edit begins.
 One standard revision round unless package says otherwise; extra revisions are billable.
 Typical editing delivery remains within the public 5-7 business-day expectation or client is proactively notified.
 Every finished project becomes an opportunity for testimonial, referral, upsell or case study.

title: Weekly Operating System
body:
The HighLife week Day Leadership / business Sales / operations Brand / content MONDAY 10:00 AM Business Meeting Scoreboard, pipeline, proposals, bookings, money, Roadmap commitments No random creative meeting TUESDAY Execution day Outbound, tours, proposals, follow-up, client sessions, editing Repurpose Sunday content WEDNESDAY 5:30 PM Team Meeting Training, accountability, bookings, client issues, engineer/intern coordination Announcements + culture THURSDAY Execution day Pipeline conversion, partnerships, stale-lead blitz, production Publish/repurpose FRIDAY Close the loop Collections, final proposals, delivery QA, next-week bookings, metric capture Event prep if applicable SATURDAY Monthly activation HL Freestyle 1x/month; event when scheduled Music/community capture SUNDAY 4:00 PM Brand Meeting Content production block before meeting HL Podcast weekly; podcast commercials 2x/month;
Music/Media/Merch priority decisions Sunday rule Batch the content, not the meetings. Shoot the weekly HL Podcast and scheduled commercials on Sunday, then use the 4:00 PM Brand Meeting to decide what the brand does next - not to recap business metrics that belong on Monday.
Weekly commitment rule  Every Monday, each leadership owner leaves with no more than 3-5 critical commitments for the week.
 Every commitment has one owner and one due date in the Roadmap.
 If a task has no owner, it is not a task; it is an idea.
 Status updates should be visible in the Roadmap. Meeting time is for decisions, blockers and accountability.
 Any initiative that does not support a quarterly OKR goes to Backlog unless it is an operational emergency.

title: Meeting Playbooks
body:
Three meetings, three different jobs Monday 10:00 AM - Business / Leadership (60-75 min) Block Time Agenda
1. Scoreboard 10 min Cash collected vs target; podcast revenue/MRR; music revenue; bookings;
major wins/misses.
2. Sales funnel 15 min Leads, tours booked/showed, proposals, close rate, stuck deals, follow-up, marketing report.
3. Operations 10 min Upcoming bookings, delivery backlog, client issues, engineer/room capacity, quality.
4. People 5 min Intern/team progress, staffing needs, accountability concerns.
5. Money 10 min Spend, ad budget, commissions, collections, unusual expense, cash needs.
6. Roadmap + SOP 10 min Quarter OKRs, blocked tasks, SOP progress, decisions needed.
7. Commit 10 min Owner + due date for the 3-5 most important commitments each.
This agenda incorporates the whiteboard list: ops, recap, upcoming tasks, bookings, revenue vs. target, Roadmap check, intern/team progress, media check, marketing check-in, budget/spend and SOPs - but orders them around the scoreboard first.
Wednesday 5:30 PM - Team (45-60 min)  Wins and recognition - 5 min.
 This week / next week bookings and event needs - 10 min.
 Client-service or technical issues that everyone can learn from - 10 min.
 Training topic / SOP of the week - 15 min.
 Intern assignments, engineer accountability and team responsibilities - 10 min.
 Announcements, culture and questions - 5 min.
Sunday 4:00 PM - Brand (45-60 min)  Rank Music, Media and Merch 1-3 for the coming week based on the quarter plan.
 Review what is being published from the content bank.
 Decide the next HL Podcast, freestyle, commercial or campaign creative priorities.
 Review upcoming monthly event and the primary business objective.
 Make creative decisions; assign owners; stop before it becomes a second Monday business meeting.
Meeting hygiene No meeting should exist just to say what happened. Use the Roadmap and HighLevel for status. Meetings exist to interpret numbers, solve blockers, make decisions and assign commitments.

title: Content + Event Cadence
body:
Create consistently without becoming a content factory Owned content cadence Format Cadence Primary job Capture day HL Podcast 1x/week Owned media, authority, network and a repeatable source of short-form content Sunday Podcast commercials 2x/month Demand generation for the podcast revenue engine Sunday HL Freestyle 1x/month Music credibility, artist community and culture Saturday Monthly event 1x/month; eventually 2x Revenue + leads + community + content Variable Event menu Event format Primary goal Secondary outcomes Podcast Mixer Qualified podcast pipeline Referrals, partnerships, testimonials, client community HL Merch Pop-Up Validate product and identity Content, email/SMS list, collaborations Aux Battle Music community and sponsor-friendly programming Artist acquisition, content, ticket/bar/vendor revenue Content Event Create high-volume content and bring creators together Leads, collaborations, owned media Release Party Artist service + event revenue Music retention, community, brand association Every event must pass the four-output test $ REVENUE Did it make or protect money?
LEADS ACQUISITION Did it create qualified relationships?
CONTENT MEDIA Did it create reusable assets?
COMMUNITY BRAND Did it deepen HighLife relevance?
An event does not need to win all four categories, but it should have one explicit primary goal and at least one secondary win. Track revenue and direct costs even when the event is intentionally a marketing investment.
Merch rule Keep merch light until demand is obvious Use limited drops, preorders, collaborations and event-linked merchandise. Avoid tying cash up in large inventory while podcasting is the capital engine.

title: Monthly Management
body:
Turn the first Monday into the monthly review The first Monday business meeting of each month becomes a 90-minute Monthly Business Review. It replaces a separate extra meeting; the weekly rhythm stays intact.
Monthly review scorecard Area Questions to answer Revenue What did we collect? By music, podcast recording, post- production, on-location, events and merch?
Podcast MRR How much contracted recurring value did we enter and exit the month with? How many active recurring clients?
Sales How many leads, tours, shows, proposals, first sales and recurring conversions? Which channel created them?
Marketing What did we spend? CPL, CAC, creative winners/losers, outbound performance and next tests?
Operations Room utilization, editing turnaround, revisions, complaints, late deliveries and capacity risks?
Brand Did we hit HL Podcast, commercials, freestyle and event cadence? What created leads or meaningful reach?
People Who is carrying too much? Who is ready for more responsibility?
What training is needed?
Finance Cash balance, receivables, commissions, upcoming fixed obligations and unusual spend?
Next month One numeric revenue target, one funnel target, one operating target and the key brand priorities.
Monthly event review  Attendance / registrations / no-shows.
 Event revenue and direct cost.
 Qualified leads and tours booked from the event.
 Content assets created.
 Sponsor/vendor relationships created or deepened.
 Would we run this event format again? If yes, what changes?
Monthly finance structure Revenue lines Direct costs / COGS Operating expenses Music sessions Engineer labor / payouts Rent Podcast recording Production labor Software / HighLevel / subscriptions Podcast post-production Editor / contractor labor Marketing / ad spend On-location production Travel / crew / rentals Insurance / admin Events Venue / security / production / talent General payroll / management Merch Product manufacturing / fulfillment Professional services / misc.
Financial discipline: Build a separate P&L view by business line. The company cannot know what to scale until it knows contribution margin by music, podcast, event and merch. Revenue alone is not enough.

title: Quarterly Okrs
body:
Three company objectives per quarter. No more.
HighLife should run quarterly planning with a maximum of three company objectives. Pillar work supports the company objectives rather than creating twenty competing OKRs. The Roadmap should tag every meaningful project to one of the three.
OKR architecture Objective Always answers Typical KRs O1 - Revenue engine How are we growing durable revenue? Revenue, podcast MRR, recurring clients, close rate, channel economics O2 - Operating system Can the team deliver the growth reliably? Turnaround, SOPs, Roadmap use, utilization, retention, staffing O3 - Brand / cultural footprint Are Music, Media and Merch getting stronger without derailing O1?
HL Podcast, freestyles, events, proof content, partnerships, merch tests OKR scoring At quarter-end, score each KR 0.0-1.0. A quarter is not a failure because every KR was not 1.0. The purpose is to force prioritization and learn what moved the business.

title: Quarter-By-Quarter Plan
body:
Launch Sprint: Aug. 10 - Sep. 30, 2026 O1 - Prove the podcast acquisition-to-recurring funnel  KR1: Book at least 50 podcast tours during the sprint.
 KR2: Achieve at least 65% tour show rate and 25% tour-to-first-sale close rate.
 KR3: Close at least 10 new paid podcast customers.
 KR4: Exit September with at least $2.5K in podcast MRR or equivalent contracted monthly recurring value.
 KR5: Every lead and opportunity lives in HighLevel with stage, owner, source and next action.

 KR2: Move all leadership commitments into the Roadmap with owner, due date and OKR tag.
 KR3: Publish the first 7 core SOPs: lead response, tour, proposal/follow-up, client onboarding, podcast session, file handoff/editing, revision/delivery.

 KR2: Complete at least 3 podcast commercial creative batches during the partial two-month sprint.
 KR3: Run 2 HL Freestyle activations and 2 monthly events or documented equivalent if calendar constraints require one event to shift.
Sprint revenue checkpoint $16K cumulative target from Aug. 10 through Sep. 30. The point of this sprint is not maximum scale; it is proving the system before Q4.

 KR2: Exit December at approximately $13K monthly revenue.

 KR5: Reach >=35% first-sale-to-recurring conversion for qualified podcast clients.

 KR2: Implement standardized briefs, file naming, edit templates and revision tracking.
 KR3: Complete a service cost study for every podcast package before expanding paid spend materially.

 KR2: 6 podcast commercial batches, 3 HL Freestyles and 3 events.
 KR3: Capture at least 6 usable client testimonials/case-study assets.
EOY 2026 decision gate: Rockville Question Data required Keep, renew, expand, buy or exit? Trailing 3-month location revenue and contribution margin Is Rockville strategically essential? Unique clients, utilization, overflow value, geographic reach Is the capital better used elsewhere? Lease obligations, buildout needs, podcast/media growth opportunities What is the 12-month forecast? Bookings, music ceiling, potential alternative use of space

Q1 2027 - Retention and recurring revenue O1 - Collect $43K and deepen recurring podcast revenue  KR1: Collect $43K total revenue in Q1.
 KR2: Exit March at $15K monthly revenue.
 KR3: Reach $5K-$6K podcast MRR / contracted recurring value.
 KR4: Maintain at least 6 active recurring podcast accounts or equivalent revenue concentration.
O2 - Make client retention a system  KR1: Measure 30-, 60- and 90-day recurring retention; target >=80% 90-day retention after sample size is meaningful.
 KR2: Install monthly client check-ins for higher-tier recurring accounts.
 KR3: Reduce avoidable revision and missed-deadline causes month over month.
O3 - Turn HighLife content into authority  KR1: 13 HL Podcast episodes, 6 podcast commercial batches, 3 freestyles and 3 events.
 KR2: Build a reusable proof library: client clips, testimonials, behind-the-scenes and final outputs tagged by ICP.

Q2 2027 - Diversify acquisition and add operational leverage O1 - Collect $47K and reach $6K-$7K+ podcast monthly revenue  KR1: Collect $47K in Q2.
 KR2: Exit June at $16K monthly revenue.
 KR3: Build at least 8 active recurring podcast clients or equivalent recurring revenue book.
 KR4: At least 30% of new podcast revenue comes from referrals, organic, partnerships or events rather than paid acquisition alone.
O2 - Add leverage where workload proves the need  KR1: Assign or hire a dedicated podcast client-success/producer owner if the trigger is reached.
 KR2: Establish an editor bench with backup capacity and consistent templates.
 KR3: Have monthly financial reporting with revenue and direct cost by business line.
O3 - Strengthen HighLife as an ecosystem  KR1: Maintain owned-content and event cadence without missing revenue service standards.
 KR2: Run at least one merch preorder/collaboration test tied to a proven community moment rather than speculative inventory.

Q3 2027 - Scale what has proven itself O1 - Collect $52K and push podcast toward $8K-$9K/month  KR1: Collect $52K in Q3.
 KR2: Exit September at $18K monthly revenue.
 KR3: Reach $8K-$9K monthly podcast/media revenue with at least 50% coming from recurring clients.
 KR4: Increase average podcast account value through packages and upsells without increasing avoidable churn.
O2 - Make a data-based capacity decision  KR1: Track sellable podcast hours, prime-time utilization, edit load and lead-to-booking wait time every month.
 KR2: Only build a second podcast room/business case if utilization and waitlist thresholds have been sustained.
 KR3: Ensure no single recurring client represents a dangerous percentage of podcast revenue.
O3 - Expand brand partnerships  KR1: Build 3-5 active referral/brand/community partnerships that create measurable leads or content opportunities.
 KR2: Continue 1 event/month; test 2/month only if team capacity and event scorecards justify it.

Q4 2027 - Finish the goal and prepare the next era O1 - Finish $250K cumulative and exit with a stronger run-rate  KR1: Collect $56K in Q4 and finish at least $250K cumulative since Aug. 10, 2026.
 KR2: Exit December at $19K base monthly revenue; stretch toward $20K-$25K.
 KR3: Reach $9K-$12K+ monthly podcast/media revenue with at least 60% recurring where feasible.
 KR4: Finish 2027 with a clear 2028 budget, revenue target and reinvestment plan.
O2 - Make the company less founder-dependent  KR1: Core sales, client-success, studio and delivery SOPs work without Jaco or JoJo manually touching every step.
 KR2: Role scorecards exist for every recurring contractor/leader.
 KR3: Bookkeeping/CPA reporting cadence and cash reserve policy are active.
O3 - Decide where the cash engine invests next  KR1: Choose 2028 priority investments across owned media, music projects, merch, events and physical capacity based on 2027 returns.
 KR2: Publish a new three-year roadmap that converts the five-year cultural vision into specific bets.

title: Weekly Scoreboard
body:
Measure a small set of numbers relentlessly Category Weekly metric Definition / use REVENUE Cash collected Primary scoreboard against monthly target.
REVENUE Podcast revenue Recording + post + package revenue collected.
REVENUE Podcast MRR Contracted monthly recurring value on active recurring accounts.
REVENUE Music revenue Protect the existing studio base and detect declines early.
SALES Leads by source Paid, outbound, referral, organic, event.
SALES Tours booked / showed Measures calendar volume and show rate.
SALES Tour-to-first-sale close Shows whether tour and offer work.
SALES First-sale-to-recurring Shows whether the business is becoming durable.
MARKETING Spend / CPL / CAC Controls growth economics by channel.
OPS Podcast room hours Measures actual utilization, not anecdotes.
OPS Turnaround time Average and % inside service standard.
OPS Revision rate Flags bad briefs, editing quality or scope creep.
BRAND Cadence completed HL Podcast / commercial / freestyle / event.
PEOPLE Roadmap commitments completed Accountability without adding more meetings.
Monday scoreboard thresholds Metric Green Yellow Red Revenue vs monthly pace >=100% pace 90%-99% <90% Tour show rate >=70% 60%-69% <60% Tour close rate >=30% 20%-29% <20% Recurring conversion >=40% 25%-39% <25% Standard edit turnaround <=5-7 days 8-9 days 10+ days Roadmap commitments >=85% on time 70%-84% <70% Thresholds should be recalibrated after 60-90 days of real data. The important part is consistency: HighLife should use the same definitions every week so trends mean something.

title: Team + Leadership Design
body:
Grow leverage before hierarchy Current operating structure Role Primary ownership Jaco - CEO Strategy, revenue target, key sales/partnerships, marketing partner oversight, finance decisions, Monday leadership meeting, brand direction.
JoJo - Founder / President / Lead Engineer Studio operations, production quality, engineer leadership, delivery systems, Wednesday team meeting, creative/technical standards.
Marketing + Sales Partner Paid ads, AI outbound, HighLevel, landing pages/automation, pipeline generation, follow-up and sales conversion; 15% first- sale commission.
Engineers / Producers Client experience, technical execution, on-time sessions, quality, upsell signals, retention.
Intern Team Research, outreach support, content/admin tasks, event support and project execution under clear owners.
Hiring / contractor triggers Need Trigger Preferred structure first Bookkeeping / CPA Immediately or as soon as monthly reporting is inconsistent Fractional bookkeeper + CPA/tax advisor; do not wait for a full-time finance hire.
Pipeline coordinator / closer Tour volume stays high and routine follow-up consumes founder time Commission / part-time contractor with clear CRM scorecard.
Podcast producer / client success 8-10+ recurring accounts or follow-ups begin slipping Part-time / contractor, then full-time when economics support it.
Editor bench Delivery pushes beyond 7 business days or one editor becomes a bottleneck Contract bench with standardized templates and QA.
Operations manager Revenue >$20K/month for several months and founders are still the routing layer Hire only after SOPs exist so the role manages a system, not chaos.
Equity and board guidance Do not give away ownership to solve a staffing problem Use cash, commission and contractor structures for normal work. Consider equity only for a long-term executive- level operator who materially changes company value, with vesting, a cliff, role/KPI expectations and legal counsel. If HighLife wants outside wisdom now, form an informal advisory circle rather than a formal board with governance power.
A useful advisory circle could include entertainment/media, finance/CPA, legal, sales/brand and DMV business/community expertise. Meet quarterly or semi-annually and bring them specific decisions, not routine updates.

title: Roadmap App + Execution System
body:
HighLevel tracks customers. Roadmap tracks the company.
The HighLife Roadmap should be the living operating layer for priorities, OKRs and commitments. It should not become a second CRM and should not duplicate every lead or booking already in HighLevel.
Every Roadmap item should contain Field Purpose Task / project Clear verb + outcome, not vague topic.
Owner Exactly one accountable person.
Pillar Revenue/Podcast, Music, Media, Merch, Events, Operations or Finance.
Quarter / OKR What company objective the work supports.
Priority 1 / 2 / 3 or Critical / Standard / Backlog.
Due date Real date; recurring tasks get recurrence.
Status Not started, In progress, Blocked, Done.
KPI / impact Revenue, funnel, operational or brand metric affected.
Dependency What must happen first or who is blocking it.
Notes / evidence Link to SOP, file, decision or result.
Recommended Roadmap views  THIS WEEK - leadership commitments due before next Monday.
 QUARTERLY OKRs - objectives, KRs, score and linked projects.
 REVENUE PROJECTS - offer, funnel, campaigns, partnerships and pricing tests.
 CONTENT CALENDAR - HL Podcast, commercial batches, freestyle and event deliverables.
 EVENTS - event date, primary goal, owner, budget, checklist and scorecard.
 SOP LIBRARY - status of processes being documented.
 BLOCKED - every item waiting on a decision, person or dependency.
 DECISION LOG - important decisions such as Rockville, new hires, package changes or new room capacity.
Roadmap rule If it is discussed Monday and needs action, it goes into the Roadmap before the meeting ends. If it is a lead, customer or sales follow-up, it stays in HighLevel.

title: Sop Library
body:
Document the work in the order revenue touches it First 12 SOPs to build Priority SOP Owner suggestion 1 New lead response + qualification Marketing/Sales 2 Podcast tour experience Jaco + Sales 3 Proposal + follow-up sequence Marketing/Sales 4 Recurring package close + autopay Jaco + Sales 5 Podcast client onboarding Podcast Producer / JoJo 6 Podcast room setup + preflight JoJo / Engineers 7 Session execution + client experience Engineers 8 File naming, backup + delivery handoff JoJo / Editors 9 Video edit + QA + revision Editing lead 10 Recurring client success + renewal Client Success 11 Monthly event playbook Leadership / Event owner 12 Monday / Wednesday / Sunday meeting process Jaco + JoJo Simple SOP format  Purpose - why this process exists.
 Trigger - what starts the process.
 Owner - one accountable role.
 Inputs - information/files needed.
 Steps - 5-12 clear actions with screenshots/links only where useful.
 Quality check - what must be true before completion.
 SLA - expected timing.
 Escalation - what happens when something goes wrong.
 Version / last updated - keep it living.
Do not spend weeks writing perfect manuals. Build the SOP while the task is being done, test it with an intern or engineer, then improve the confusing parts.

title: Capital Allocation + Risk
body:
Protect cash while the engine is still proving itself Capital priorities Priority Rule
1. Keep the lights on Maintain enough cash to cover fixed obligations and avoid growth decisions made from panic.
2. Measure margins Know direct cost and contribution margin by service before scaling ad spend or discounting packages.
3. Fund what converts Reinvest in campaigns, sales systems, editors and capacity only when the scoreboard shows a return.
4. Build a reserve Work toward 2-3 months of fixed operating expenses before major expansion.
5. Invest in pillars from profit Use podcast profits, not gross revenue, to fund larger Music/Media/Merch bets.
Major risks and mitigations Risk How it shows up Mitigation Founder concentration Jaco/JoJo become the routing layer for every decision SOPs, role scorecards, Roadmap, triggered contractor hires.
Lead volume without sales discipline Many tours, few payments Same-day proposal, sales coaching, funnel KPIs and call/tour review.
Sales without retention First-sale revenue rises but MRR stays flat Recurring offer, client-success cadence, reserved slots and renewal process.
Post-production bottleneck Late edits and revision chaos Editor bench, templates, briefs, QA and capacity thresholds.
Too-broad ICP Ads generate low-budget or low-intent leads Qualifying language, persona-specific creative, lead scoring.
Creative distraction Events/merch/media consume leadership time without returns Quarterly OKRs, 65% growth allocation and event scorecards.
Expansion too early Second room or major gear purchase drains cash Utilization trigger and business case before capital spend.
Capital discipline The company should feel underbuilt before it expands physical capacity. A busy calendar is not enough; prove sustained utilization, waitlist pressure, healthy margins and delivery capacity first.

title: 90-Day Execution Plan
body:
The first 12 weeks Week Primary objective Deliverable 1 Install the scoreboard Baseline current revenue, MRR, lead sources, tours, show rate, close rate, room hours and turnaround. Roadmap updated.
2 Finalize offer ladder Cost-check recurring packages; create one- page package sheet and tour close options.
3 Fix the tour-to-proposal flow Tour checklist, discovery questions, same- day proposal template and follow-up automation.
4 Launch recurring conversion Every first-session client receives a relevant recurring option; measure conversion.
5 Build ad creative system Use first commercial batch to create multiple hooks/personas; track campaign-to-revenue attribution.
6 Build referral engine Create referral ask, partner list and intro offer for agencies, professionals and existing clients.
7 Run event as acquisition Monthly event with QR/CRM capture, clear primary KPI and post-event tour offer.
8 Harden client success Kickoff brief, reserved slots, delivery checklist, testimonial/referral moment.
9 Coach sales with data Review lost tours, objections and proposals;
improve script/offer instead of just buying more leads.
10 Build the proof library Organize testimonials, best clips, BTS, set photos and use cases by ICP for ads and tours.
11 Cost + capacity review Measure editor hours, margin, room utilization, revision rate and delivery backlog.
12 Quarter review + next OKRs Score KRs, keep/kill experiments, set next- quarter targets and update Roadmap.
What should be true after 90 days  HighLife knows exactly where every podcast lead is in the funnel.
 Tours have a repeatable discovery and closing flow.
 Recurring packages are being sold and retention is measured.
 Monday leadership decisions are based on one scoreboard.
 The Roadmap contains current OKRs, owners and due dates.
 At least the first 12 revenue-critical SOPs are drafted or actively being built.
 Content and events run on cadence without stealing the company from revenue execution.
 Leadership can say which channel, offer and client type creates the best economics.

title: Decision Rules
body:
The HighLife guardrails Rule Meaning
1. Podcast is the cash engine through 2027 Unless data disproves the thesis, 60%-70% of growth energy goes here.
2. Three quarterly objectives maximum New ideas compete for backlog unless they directly support an OKR.
3. Every task gets one owner Shared ownership usually means no ownership.
4. No second room before capacity proof Use utilization and waitlist data, not excitement.
5. No large merch inventory without demand proof Use preorder/limited-drop tests.
6. Every event has a primary KPI Revenue, leads, content or community - know why it exists.
7. Sell recurring before discounting Increase account value through service depth and convenience.
8. Track profit drivers, not just revenue Direct labor, commission, ad spend and revision load determine what is worth scaling.
9. Protect the brand Premium price requires premium reliability, communication and final output.
10. Reinvest from strength Podcast profit should fund larger Music, Media and Merch bets after the core machine is healthy.
The weekly question What is the single highest-leverage thing HighLife can do this week to increase durable revenue without damaging quality or the brand?
